analysis: I found no concrete security regressions in the supplied units. docs/reports/README.md only adds an index entry (head line 7, 2026-10-15-bonsai9b-publication.md) and a header date. The remaining changes are index reordering and link shifts. I did not check that the new relative link target exists. The only security-relevant pre-existing statements are the retained pins and the platform-owned evidence links at head lines 117-118, and those are unchanged. scripts/test_model_registry_workflow.py is a new test that extracts the 'run: |' blocks from .github/workflows/register-model.yml by step name. It runs them under bash -e -u -o pipefail against a loopback ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1. The environment is os.environ minus AWS_*/R2_*, with NO_PROXY set and a fixture key. No real credential is sent, and the test only talks to loopback. It asserts that the revision-only path (/v1/admin/models/{id}%2F.../publish-revision) sends only version and hugging_face_artifact, that HTTP 503 and a missing key fail, that a malformed artifact stops before any POST, and that the workflow has no R2/AWS secrets. The workflow file itself is not in the supplied units, so its actual permissions, secret handling, input injection (e.g. ${{ inputs.* }} interpolated into shell) and the coordinator admin endpoint authorization are unverified. The MODEL_REGISTRY_PUBLISHING_KEY admin credential and the HF revision pinning relate to A-004, T-012 and T-027 (weight substitution), but the coordinator backend is out of scope for this repo's threat model. The integration pass should check the workflow YAML if it is available. No threat-model update is needed from these units.
